summary: Franklin County, PA lookout: the register calls it a bald tower used 1908 to about 1917, no longer standing; Forest Lookouts calls it an open observation point.

facts.design: bald tower (register); open observation point (Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: Register says no longer standing; no source describes what remains at the site today

visit.trail_note: Chimney Rocks is a hiking circuit in Michaux State Forest (Appalachian, Shaffer Rock and Hermitage trails) with a trailhead on Rattlesnake Run Road; no source ties the lookout site to that circuit

events.note: Register says the bald tower was used from 1908
Register says use ended circa 1917; Forest Lookouts says an open observation point was set up before 1918, which conflicts with a built tower
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: bald tower used from 1908 to about 1917 and no longer standing
evidence.quote: This bald tower was used from 1908 to circa 1917 and is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: no longer standing (no description of the site today)

evidence.quote: An open observation point established prior to 1918.

evidence.supports: Chimney Rocks is a circuit of the Appalachian Trail, Shaffer Rock Trail and Hermitage Trail
evidence.quote: The Chimney Rocks is a circuit composed of the Appalachian Trail, Shaffer Rock Trail, and the Hermitage Trail.

evidence.supports: the circuit is in Michaux State Forest
evidence.quote: outdoor adventures in Michaux State Forest

evidence.supports: one trailhead is on Rattlesnake Run Road
evidence.quote: we chose to begin at Rattlesnake Run Road

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says a bald tower used 1908 to about 1917; Forest Lookouts says an open observation point set up before 1918. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

sources.title: Treasury of Boulder Caves and a Majestic Vista at Michaux Chimney Rocks

notes_for_editor: Thin record: three short pages, no photo, and the register gives no coordinates. The brief's coordinates (39.8162, -77.46999) sit near the pinnacle of the Chimney Rocks formation (39.81897, -77.47108 in the Hemlock State Explorer page), but no source ties the lookout to that spot, so check before using them. Do not merge with the separate Chimney Rocks Tower Site (Perry County), US 242 / PA 71.
